neet_che_u09_t02_1.working: A non-metal does not have a metallic radius. Its cation would be smaller than the neutral atom. The van der Waals radius is half the distance between non-bonded atoms, so it exceeds the covalent radius and is the largest.

neet_che_u09_t02_2.working: All four species have 10 electrons. Nuclear charge rises in the order N(7) < F(9) < Na(11) < Al(13). A higher nuclear charge pulls the same electrons closer, so radius decreases in that order: N3- > F- > Na+ > Al3+.

neet_che_u09_t02_3.working: The covalent radius is half the bond length: 198/2 = 99 pm.

neet_che_u09_t02_4.working: Ga (about 135 pm) is smaller than Al (about 143 pm), so A is true. This happens because 3d electrons shield the nucleus poorly, not effectively, so R is false.

neet_che_u09_t02_5.working: Noble gas radii are van der Waals radii, which are large, so they are not the smallest in their periods; I is false. Zr and Hf have nearly equal radii because of the lanthanoid contraction; II is true.
